blocks.text: Unusually detailed module docstring explains the exact Starlette middleware stack order that causes the CORS-less 500, why @app.exception_handler(Exception) doesn't help, and why UnhandledErrorMiddleware sits inside CORSMiddleware. Also documents the two CORS origin env vars and why allow_credentials is never configurable.
blocks.title: Module docstring — the problem and the fix

blocks.text: INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL is the fixed generic message all 500 responses carry. DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS lists both loopback spellings (localhost and 127.0.0.1) because browsers treat them as distinct origins.
blocks.title: Module-level constants

blocks.text: parse_allowed_origins splits on commas, strips whitespace, discards empty items, and falls back to defaults if nothing remains. parse_allowed_origin_regex strips whitespace and returns None for a blank value. Both are module-level functions so they can be unit-tested without booting a server.
blocks.title: CORS origin parsers

blocks.text: Pure-ASGI class (not BaseHTTPMiddleware) to avoid buffering. __call__ only acts on HTTP scopes; websocket and lifespan pass straight through. It wraps send with a closure that tracks whether http.response.start has been seen, so it only attempts a JSON 500 if headers haven't gone out yet, then always re-raises.
blocks.title: UnhandledErrorMiddleware implementation

blocks.text: add_cors_and_error_middleware compiles the regex at call time to catch invalid patterns at boot, then adds UnhandledErrorMiddleware then CORSMiddleware. The comment explains the counter-intuitive ordering: add first = innermost, add last = outermost. Credentials are hardcoded off.
blocks.title: Wiring function

gotchas: The last middleware added is the outermost — that's why UnhandledErrorMiddleware must be added BEFORE CORSMiddleware in add_cors_and_error_middleware
If the response has already started (streaming response that fails mid-stream), no 500 is sent — it's too late to change the status
INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL is a fixed generic string; the original exception message is never included in the response body
how_it_works: add_cors_and_error_middleware adds UnhandledErrorMiddleware first (inner), then CORSMiddleware (outer), so error responses travel outward through CORS
UnhandledErrorMiddleware wraps send in a tracking closure to know whether headers have already been sent
On an unhandled exception it sends a JSONResponse({detail: INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL}) only if the response hasn't started yet, then always re-raises to preserve uvicorn logging and Sentry capture
parse_allowed_origins splits on commas, strips whitespace, falls back to DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS when nothing is left
allow_credentials is hardcoded False and not configurable; the docstring explains why
outputs: JSON 500 response with detail string on unhandled exceptions; CORS headers on all responses via CORSMiddleware
purpose: Solves a Starlette middleware ordering problem: unhandled exceptions escape past CORSMiddleware and reach ServerErrorMiddleware, which writes a bare 500 without CORS headers. The browser then sees an opaque network error instead of the real status and message. UnhandledErrorMiddleware sits just inside CORSMiddleware and catches whatever the route layer didn't handle, writing a JSON 500 that the CORS layer then stamps with the correct Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
side_effects: re-raises caught exceptions (uvicorn logs, Sentry captures)
compiles allowed_origin_regex at boot to fail early on invalid patterns
